rule: Create temporary/scratch files freely without prompting the founder for permission first.
Prefer a witty/contradiction-of-expectation title over the formulaic 'It is X, not Y' construction for all content titles.
check: lint-rule regex matching the specific banned formula pattern (e.g. "X, not Y" / "it's not X, it's Y") in a draft title
misses: paraphrased or reworded formulaic titles that avoid the exact syntax, and cannot judge whether a passing title is actually witty/good

rule: Before writing or keeping a tool, classify it ENFORCE/COMPUTE (keep) vs RE-EXPOSE (delete a wrapper that just re-exposes a CLI the model already uses well), and measure rather than assume before instructing a harness to prefer one tool over another.
Keep an explicit, session-independent list of all active workstreams (including failures) and persist load-bearing items to durable stores rather than relying on conversation memory.
Treat every claim (status field, subagent 'done', vendor benchmark, config flag) as unverified until backed by a reproducible artifact; verify in proportion to cost-if-wrong.
Never declare a background agent dead from silence alone; verify liveness (ps/task status) and TaskStop it before relaunching, to avoid spawning duplicate background work.
check: PreToolUse hook on TaskCreate that queries TaskList for an existing alive task with a matching identifier/description and blocks or warns before allowing a duplicate dispatch
misses: semantically duplicate tasks phrased differently (no exact identifier match), and legitimate intentional relaunches after a genuinely-confirmed death via an out-of-band check

rule: Never ship an AI-delegated fix unverified — spot-check the technical/factual claims in a subagent's applied fix before accepting it, since fixing the flagged issue can introduce a new false claim.

When re-reviewing a finding/design that already survived a self-correction round, instruct reviewers to explicitly try to reject the premise outright (REJECT/DEFEND verdict) rather than just list issues, then still independently verify the panel's most serious claims forensically.

Before accepting any fix to a detector/guard/gate, explicitly determine which direction the fix now errs (state it) and brief the verifier to attack that specific inversion by name, preferring a fix that requires agreement between signals over one that lets one signal override another.

On recognizing the amdgpu wedge symptom cluster (rocm-smi hangs, GPU containers stuck in D-state / undead, exit 42 with disk not full), go straight to a hard power cycle instead of attempting a soft systemctl reboot, which will hang.
check: wrapper-script/monitoring probe that checks rocm-smi responsiveness and container D-state before choosing reboot method, escalating straight to hard power cycle when the known symptom cluster matches
misses: novel or partial symptom presentations that don't match the exact known cluster, and the judgment call of how long to wait before concluding a reboot is truly hung

rule: A benchmark task passing static thin/half/full calibration is not sufficient evidence it discriminates models; validate discrimination against a real-model panel at registration time and flag 'all models score the same' as non-discriminating, and require a precedent-inconsistency variant before generalizing a difficulty finding.
check: CI-job at task registration that runs a real-model panel and computes score variance/spread across models, flagging zero (or near-zero) variance as non-discriminating
misses: weak-but-nonzero discrimination (borderline variance), and the precedent-consistency variant requirement, which needs a human/domain judgment to design and cannot itself be generated deterministically

rule: Before trusting an enumeration-based uniqueness certificate as evidence a benchmark task requires induction, build and run a zero-induction falsifier that enumerates the closed candidate space directly; if it scores comparably to a genuine actor, the task must be rejected as non-inductive.
check: a zero-induction enumeration falsifier (itertools.permutations over the closed candidate space, keep the inhabitant matching stated constraints) run against the task at registration; reject the task if its score matches real-actor performance

rule: Smoke-probe a CLI harness's real capability with one trivial live task before fanning out on an assumption it can/can't do something, and require gates in a workflow to carry an evidence_backed boolean alongside any verdict so fire-and-forget forwarder results (structurally complete but evidence-empty) can't silently pass a merge/rollout gate.
check: schema-constraint requiring the verdict object to include a populated evidence_backed field before a merge/rollout gate proceeds
misses: a fabricated or falsely-set evidence_backed=true with no real evidence behind it, and the smoke-probe-before-fanout step itself, which has no deterministic check
